chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

O Allah, to You is the praise. I praise You and seek Your assistance, and You are my Lord and I am Your servant. I have entered the morning upon Your covenant and Your promise, and I believe in Your promise and fulfill Your covenant to the best of my ability. And there is no power and no strength except with Allah, Alone, without partner, and I testify that Muhammad is His servant and His Messenger.

I have entered the morning upon the fitrah of Islam, and the phrase of monotheism, and the religion of Ibrahim, and the religion of Muhammad. Upon that I live and die, if Allah wills. O Allah, keep me alive as long as You keep me alive with it, and cause me to die when You cause me to die upon it, and resurrect me when You resurrect me upon it, seeking Your pleasure and following Your path. To You I turn my back, and to You I delegate my affairs.

The Progeny of Muhammad are my Imams, there is no Imam for me other than them. By them I follow, and them I befriend, and by them I am guided. O Allah, make them my guardians in this world and the Hereafter, and make me a friend of their friends and an enemy of their enemies in this world and the Hereafter, and join me with the righteous, and my fathers with them.
ai.seo_question: What is the morning supplication for affirming the covenant and the Imams in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This supplication, known as Du'a al-Sahar or the Morning Adhkar, is a cornerstone of daily Shia devotional practice, emphasizing the renewal of one's covenant (Ahd) with Allah each morning. It uniquely integrates theological monotheism with the specific Shia doctrine of Imamah, explicitly invoking the Ahl al-Bayt as the primary guides and intercessors for the believer. The text reflects the scholarly emphasis on maintaining spiritual continuity from evening to morning through constant remembrance and alignment with the Fitrah of Islam.
